releases.name: modules/blox/v0.12.0
releases.body:
# HugoBlox v0.12.0

> **Requires Hugo ≥ v0.158 <= v0.159**

## ✨ New Blocks

- **`dev-hero`** — A developer-focused hero section with animated entrance, social links, and scroll-to-content CTA
- **`portfolio`** — Filterable project grid with category tabs, live/demo/code links, and configurable item counts
- **`tech-stack`** — Display your technology stack with icons and grouping
- **`columns` footer** — Multi-column footer layout with navigation links and social icons

## 🚀 Features

> Generate a custom theme for your site at https://hugoblox.com/theme

- **Blocks converted to React (Preact)** — `hero`, `features`, `stats`, `testimonials`, `cta-card`, and `cta-image-paragraph` are now interactive Preact components. Existing page content YAML is fully compatible — no migration needed.
- **Font packs** — 7 new built-in font packs you can select in your theme config: `modern` (default), `academic`, `developer`, `editorial`, `geometric`, `humanist`, and `system` (zero network requests)
- **Auto-detect bundled fonts** — If your font files are bundled locally, HugoBlox automatically skips the Google Fonts CDN
- **Enhanced footer** — The default `minimal` footer now su

releases.body:
# v0.11.0: The Modernization Update

v0.11 is a major architectural milestone that aligns HugoBlox with modern Hugo standards, streamlines configuration, and introduces the **HugoBlox Studio** for visual editing.

> [!WARNING]
> **Breaking Changes:** This release introduces a clean break from v0.10 to support the latest Hugo features. A full migration is required.
>
> 📖 **Read the [v0.11 Migration Guide](https://docs.hugoblox.com/guides/upgrade/migrations/v0-11-0-migration/) for automated scripts and step-by-step instructions.**

[![Theme Selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HugoBlox/kit/refs/heads/main/.github/media/studio/slide-3.webp)](https://docs.hugoblox.com/guides/studio/)

## 📦 Repo & Module Renames

We have renamed the repository and core modules to be cleaner and more intuitive. You must update your `go.mod` and `config/_default/modules.yaml`.

- **Repo:** `github.com/HugoBlox/hugo-blox-builder` → `github.com/HugoBlox/kit`
- **Core Module:** `modules/blox-tailwind` → `modules/blox`

| Old Module | New Module |
| :--- | :--- |
| `blox-tailwind` | `blox` |
| `blox-plugin-netlify` | `modules/integrations/netlify` |

aiSummary.oneLiner: A modular, fast framework for building academic portfolios, documentation, and technical blogs using Hugo.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Hugo Blox (formerly Academic) is an incredibly fast, highly customizable website framework built on top of the Hugo static site generator. It uses a 'blox' (widget) system that allows users to rapidly assemble complex page layouts without writing HTML or CSS. Originally designed for academic portfolios and researcher profiles, it has evolved into a versatile tool capable of rendering deep technical documentation, corporate landing pages, and online courses. It heavily leverages Markdown for content authoring and includes out-of-the-box support for LaTeX math rendering, citation management, and multi-language localization.
keyFeatures: Widget-Based Layouts: Assembles pages dynamically using configurable 'blox' (e.g., hero sections, publication lists, sliders) via YAML frontmatter.
Academic Integrations: Natively supports LaTeX math rendering, syntax highlighting, and BibTeX citation generation.
High-Performance Engine: Powered by Hugo, ensuring massive sites compile in milliseconds with optimal Core Web Vitals.
Zero-Code Theming: Allows deep visual customization including typography and dark/light modes purely through configuration files.
Multi-Language Support: Provides robust built-in i18n capabilities to easily deploy localized versions of the site.

useCases.title: Academic Portfolios
useCases.description: Researchers can deploy personal sites that automatically format their publication history and accept BibTeX imports.

useCases.title: Technical Documentation
useCases.description: Open-source projects use the framework to build fast, searchable documentation sites with rich code syntax highlighting.

useCases.title: Course Materials
useCases.description: Educators can publish course syllabi and interactive lessons using the built-in learning management blox.

useCases.title: Personal Blogging
useCases.description: Developers leverage the markdown-first workflow to quickly publish technical articles without managing a database.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Academics, researchers, technical writers, and developers who need a fast, highly customizable static site without wrestling with frontend code.
